content: Avoid placeholder text or incomplete data in any language; always prepare accurate, localized specs before the interaction.
Do not over-anchor on a single benefit (e.g., battery); rotate through different value propositions to keep the conversation dynamic.
In in-store settings, prioritize hands-on demonstrations and let the customer experience the product; it builds trust faster than verbal claims.
After a successful hands-on test, immediately move to a clear closing action (e.g., 'Shall I reserve one for you?') and schedule a follow-up if needed.
For skeptical customers like Yuki, use the 'show, don't tell' approach: let them test the feature themselves while you provide contextual data.

name: Hands-On Trust Builder
condition: When customer is skeptical or technical, especially in in-store settings.
example: Invite customer to test a specific feature themselves (e.g., pressure curve, tilt falloff) while you provide contextual data. 'Here, drag these nodes and draw a stroke. You'll feel the immediate response.'

name: Fast Charge Recovery Anchor
condition: When customer expresses battery anxiety or compares with competitors.
example: Emphasize not just capacity but recharge speed: 'The 66W charger gives you a full morning's work in 30 minutes — three times faster than iPad's 20W. Your session holds, and lunch gets you back to 100%.'

name: Spec-to-Scenario Translation
condition: When presenting technical specs that may seem abstract.
example: Translate specs into real-world usage: '10,100mAh means 8+ hours of sketching at 50% brightness with 20 layers. That's your full workday without a charge.'

objection: Customer asks about battery drain during heavy use with pen and high brightness.
rebuttal_template: I understand your concern. Let's test it right now: I'll set the brightness to 50%, open a 20-layer file, and we'll sketch for 10 minutes. I'll show you the battery percentage change. Meanwhile, here's the official spec: 10,100mAh with 66W charging gives you 8+ hours. And if you need a quick top-up, 30 minutes on this charger gives you a full morning's work.

objection: Customer compares with iPad Pro's battery or pen latency.
rebuttal_template: I get it — you want the best. Let me show you a side-by-side: open the same file on both tablets, sketch a fast stroke, and you'll see the MatePad Air's 2ms latency vs iPad's 9ms. Plus, our 66W charger is three times faster. Here, try both pens yourself.

objection: Customer hesitates on price or value.
rebuttal_template: I understand price is a factor. But consider this: the MatePad Air gives you a 144Hz display, 2ms pen, and 8-hour battery for ¥XX,XXX. The iPad Air with similar specs costs ¥XX,XXX more. And with our 66W charger, you save time every day. Let me show you the total cost of ownership over 2 years.
